teaching.hint: How does each car’s solo arrival time compare with the group already ahead of it?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: When scanning from the car closest to the target backward, a car joins an ahead fleet exactly when its solo arrival time is no later than that fleet’s arrival time.
solution_outline.approach: Sort cars by decreasing starting position. Compute their solo times to target and scan, maintaining the arrival time of the last fleet ahead; start a new fleet only when the next car’s solo time is strictly greater.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The maintained time is the arrival time of the nearest formed fleet ahead; formed fleet times increase as the scan proceeds backward.
solution_outline.correctness: A car whose solo time is no later catches the fleet ahead by the target and cannot pass it. A slower-arriving car cannot catch that fleet, so it begins a distinct fleet. The scan decides each car exactly once.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n log n)` time for sorting and `O(n)` storage for paired position and speed information.
solution_outline.pitfall: Treating equal arrival times as separate fleets violates the catch-at-target rule.

common_wrong_turns: Treat meeting exactly at the target as separate fleets
source_fidelity_notes: The no-passing and catch-at-target rules are both explicit; source examples are omitted.
